semantic_description.level_1_elemental: Nine variables representing retention dynamics, feature velocity, accumulated complexity, engineering capacity, and investment trade-offs, connected by twelve causal links arranged in four feedback loops.
semantic_description.level_2_statistical: 12 causal links across 9 variables; 4 loops total (2 reinforcing, 2 balancing); negative flows (friction-to-retention, maintenance-to-investment, retention-to-gap) create the balancing paths; positive flows dominate the system.
semantic_description.level_3_perceptual: Two competing reinforcing loops (complexity trap R1, capacity drain R2) and two balancing loops (novelty B1, core investment B2) create a dynamic tension; the reinforcing loops drive ratcheting retention decline, while the balancing loops provide weaker recovery forces, with novelty decaying fast and core investment crowded out by maintenance.
semantic_description.level_4_contextual: A software product trapped in a reinforcing cycle: high retention gap drives feature releases, which add complexity and increase maintenance burden. The complexity trap (R1) amplifies the gap through accumulated friction. Simultaneously, maintenance burden starves core-value investment (R2), further eroding retention quality. The novelty from releases provides temporary retention boost (B1), but this fast-decaying effect is overwhelmed by structural complexity damage. The only durable escape is core-value investment (B2), which the organization intellectually recognizes but operationally under-funds. The analysis deliberately excludes competitive poaching and cohort-mix effects as rival hypotheses; unless those are ruled out, the complexity loop's dominance cannot be trusted.
semantic_description.short_alt: Feature velocity drives complexity feedback trap that outpaces novelty recovery.

title: Retention Feedback System: Complexity Trap vs. Novelty Balancing
